selection_rule: Exactly twelve lawfully acquired and normalized sources selected after Part I for heterogeneity of mathematical mechanism, era, and exposition; not statistical representativeness.

sources.title: On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude
sources.version: David R. Wilkins English translation of the 1859 memoir
sources.license: Translation used by permission of David R. Wilkins; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Foundational historical source: analytic continuation, the functional equation, the explicit prime-zero relation, and Riemann's own limited statement of the conjecture.
alternatives: H. M. Edwards, Riemann's Zeta Function (1974)
E. C. Titchmarsh / D. R. Heath-Brown, The Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function

sources.title: Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
sources.version: Clay official problem description, repository PDF dated 2022-05
sources.license: No open redistribution license located; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Authoritative problem description connecting the classical analytic problem to L-functions, finite-field analogues, numerical evidence, and Weil's explicit formula while marking speculation as such.
alternatives: Peter Sarnak, Problems of the Millennium: The Riemann Hypothesis
J. Brian Conrey, Riemann's Hypothesis (2016)

sources.title: The Riemann Hypothesis
sources.license: AMS copyright; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: High-quality exposition of why several analytic and spectral viewpoints are attractive, what partial results actually show, and where natural routes remain incomplete.
alternatives: Peter Borwein et al. (eds.), The Riemann Hypothesis: A Resource for the Afficionado and Virtuoso Alike
Aleksandar Ivić, The Riemann Zeta-Function

sources.title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
sources.version: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 399, 1-26
sources.license: Publisher copyright; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Primary major partial-result paper whose mollifier construction makes a concrete representation/optimization tradeoff visible without implying RH.
alternatives: Norman Levinson, More than one-third of the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are on sigma=1/2 (1974)
S. Feng, Zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line (2012)

sources.title: An Elementary Problem Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
sources.version: American Mathematical Monthly 109(6), arXiv version math/0008177
sources.license: arXiv license not asserted as redistributable; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Arithmetic equivalent criterion that deliberately changes representation from zero location to a universal divisor-sum inequality, exposing both the attraction and limits of equivalence.
alternatives: Xian-Jin Li, The positivity of a sequence of numbers and the Riemann hypothesis (1997)
Guy Robin, Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothèse de Riemann (1984)

sources.title: A strengthening of the Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
sources.version: Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 14, arXiv math/0202141
sources.license: arXiv license not asserted as redistributable; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Function-space reformulation in which RH becomes an approximation/closure problem and a discrete sequence replaces a continuous family.
alternatives: Bertil Nyman, On some groups and semigroups of translations (1950 thesis)
Arne Beurling, A closure problem related to the Riemann zeta-function (1955)

sources.title: The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function
sources.version: Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. XXIV, 181-193; author-hosted scan
sources.license: AMS copyright; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Primary zero-statistics source introducing the pair-correlation mechanism and the spectral-eigenvalue analogy while keeping conditional inputs visible.
alternatives: A. M. Odlyzko, On the distribution of spacings between zeros of the zeta function (1987)
Zeev Rudnick and Peter Sarnak, Zeros of principal L-functions and random matrix theory (1996)

sources.title: Random Matrix Theory and zeta(1/2+it)
sources.version: Communications in Mathematical Physics 214, 57-89; HP report copy
sources.license: Publisher copyright; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Random-matrix bridge that matches matrix size to zero density, separates universal matrix statistics from arithmetic prime factors, and generates testable moment conjectures.
alternatives: J. P. Keating and N. C. Snaith, Random matrix theory and L-functions at s=1/2 (2000)
N. Katz and P. Sarnak, Random Matrices, Frobenius Eigenvalues, and Monodromy (1999)

sources.title: Trace formula in noncommutative geometry and the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
sources.license: arXiv license not asserted as redistributable; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Spectral/noncommutative program that interprets the explicit formula through a trace formula and foregrounds the difficulty of turning an absorption spectrum into the self-adjoint operator desired by Hilbert-Polya.
alternatives: M. V. Berry and J. P. Keating, The Riemann zeros and eigenvalue asymptotics (1999)
Dorian Goldfeld, Explicit formulae as trace formulae (1989)

sources.title: The De Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative
sources.version: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 8, e6; arXiv 1801.05914v3
sources.license: arXiv license not asserted as redistributable; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Heat-flow deformation turns RH into a boundary statement and proves the complementary obstruction: if RH is true, it is only barely so.
alternatives: Charles Newman and Wei Wu, Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics (2019)
Polymath 15, Effective approximation of heat-flow evolution of the Riemann xi function (2019)

sources.title: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12
sources.version: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 53, 792-797; arXiv 2004.09765v2
sources.license: arXiv license not asserted as redistributable; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Rigorous interval-arithmetic verification source that sharply separates finite certified evidence and completeness of a computation from proof of an unbounded statement.
alternatives: Alan Turing, Some calculations of the Riemann zeta-function (1953)
J. van de Lune, H. te Riele, and D. Winter, On the zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the critical strip IV (1986)

sources.title: The Riemann Hypothesis
sources.version: AIM WWN preliminary resource, 2004-06-17 hard-copy version
sources.license: No open redistribution license located; external local cache only
sources.selection_rationale: Collaborative map of L-functions, equivalent criteria, spectral attacks, and documented unsuccessful approaches; included to test extraction from intentionally unfinished reference prose.
alternatives: J. Brian Conrey, The Riemann Hypothesis (Notices AMS, 2003)
Peter Borwein et al. (eds.), The Riemann Hypothesis: A Resource for the Afficionado and Virtuoso Alike
